tasks.spec:
You are closing ONE automation gap in the OBE podcast repo at /mnt/d_drive/repos/podcast. Do NOT git commit, git push, or open a PR. Do NOT send anything externally, do not publish, and do not call Transistor, YouTube, Blotato or any provider. Do not load skills or call MCP/Apps. Subscription/OAuth only, zero API spend. PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 and PYTHONPYCACHEPREFIX=/tmp on every python call. Files you may change: server/pipeline/orchestrator.py, server/pipeline/content_qa.py, tests/test_content_qa.py and tests/test_orchestrator.py. Nothing else. Never write into episodes/.

THE GAP: episode 2026-06-10-fred-cho ran the full pipeline on 2026-07-25 and produced final/episode.mp4 (736MB), final/episode.mp3, two polished promo clips in four cuts each, content/show-notes.md and content/episode_content.json. It then PARKED at stage awaiting-host-input, blocked on content_qa. The QA record shows hard_findings: [] and style_findings: [] -- nothing mechanical was wrong. It failed ONLY the LLM voice judge: voice_match 0.72 and hook_quality 0.60 against confidence_floor 0.8, with 13 specific critiques such as 'zero contractions anywhere', 'the same quote hook is reused verbatim across posts 1 and 3', 'multi-provincial doctor shortage appears verbatim in all three posts', and 'this episode is worth 45 minutes states a runtime as fact' (the episode is 32m32s).

Why this matters more than one episode: in server/pipeline/orchestrator.py the artwork generation call (generate_episode_artwork, around line 3835), the publish preflight and the advance to publish-queued ALL sit AFTER the qa-passed advance. A content-QA park therefore blocks every remaining deliverable -- thumbnail, all artwork surfaces, preflight and the publish queue -- even though nothing is mechanically wrong with the content.

The outreach lane already solves exactly this shape: scripts/obe_draft_voice_qa.py and scripts/obe_draft_to_linear_bridge.py run voice QA WITH AUTO-REVISE before a human ever sees the draft. Episode content has no such loop: grep for revise in content_qa.py and orchestrator.py returns nothing. Read the outreach scripts first and follow their proven shape.

BUILD THIS:
1. A module constant CONTENT_QA_MAX_REVISIONS in server/pipeline/orchestrator.py, a small integer (2 is a sensible default). The loop MUST be bounded: an unbounded revise loop against a model is a budget hole.
2. A method on PipelineOrchestrator named EXACTLY:
     _revise_content_until_qa_passes(self, *, content, qa_result, regenerate, run_qa)
   `regenerate` is a callable that produces new content and MUST accept a `problems` keyword carrying the QA critiques; `run_qa` is a callable taking the content and returning a QA result dict. It returns a dict with at least {"content": <final content>, "qa": <final qa result>, "attempts": [<per-attempt record>]}. Each attempt record should carry enough to audit what was tried: the attempt number, the scores, and the critiques fed in.
3. Semantics, in this exact order:
   * If qa_result has ANY hard_findings, return immediately WITHOUT regenerating. Placeholder, banned-phrase and bad-link classes are hard-refuse and a human must see them; rewriting them would launder a defect. The same applies to style_findings unless you can argue in a comment why a style finding is safely machine-fixable, in which case say so explicitly.
   * Otherwise, while the QA has not passed and attempts remain, call regenerate(problems=<the critiques from the previous QA verdict>) and re-run run_qa. The critiques MUST be fed in: a blind retry reproduces the same voice failure and just burns tokens.
   * Stop as soon as QA passes, or when CONTENT_QA_MAX_REVISIONS is exhausted.
4. Wire it into the content-QA handling in handle_post_production_complete so a score-only failure is revised BEFORE the episode parks. If the loop ends without a pass, park exactly as today (awaiting_host_input plus the review-queue item) but include the attempt records so a human can see every attempt, its scores and its critiques.
5. Do NOT weaken the gate: the confidence floor stays, hard findings still park immediately, and only a genuinely PASSING QA may advance to qa-passed. If your change lets an episode reach qa-passed without a passing QA result, it is wrong.

TESTS to add across tests/test_content_qa.py and tests/test_orchestrator.py, all with stubs so no model is called:
  * a score-only failure that would pass on the second attempt: assert the content is regenerated, the critiques are passed into regeneration, and the episode advances to qa-passed,
  * a persistent failure: assert regeneration is bounded by CONTENT_QA_MAX_REVISIONS, the episode still parks at awaiting-host-input, and the review item carries the attempt records,
  * a hard finding: assert ZERO regenerations and an immediate park,
  * the existing tests in both files stay green.

VERIFY BEFORE YOU FINISH and paste the real output into your final message:
  cd /mnt/d_drive/repos/podcast && PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 PYTHONPYCACHEPREFIX=/tmp python3 -m pytest tests/test_content_qa.py tests/test_orchestrator.py -q -p no:cacheprovider
A claim without executed output is not done. Leave the working tree dirty -- the coordinator lands it.
tasks.verified: A content-QA failure that is only a voice/hook score now regenerates with the critiques fed back and can reach qa-passed on its own, the loop is bounded and still parks with every attempt recorded when it cannot pass, and hard findings are never auto-revised
